text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English poet and author WILLIAM BLAKE was born in 1757. He reportedly liked to sit in the garden with his wife reciting "ParadiseLost" while they were both naked.
English/Australian builder JACOB PITMAN, who introduced his brother's writing system to Australia, was born in 1810.
Australian Olympic swimmer CECIL HEALY, who founded the Manly Surf Club, was born in 1881.

American singer, pianist, composer and songwriter RANDY NEWMAN was born in 1943. At the age of 17 he had a permament job as a songwriter and was famed for his ironic songs about the 'American Way Of Life'. He had his own hit with "Short People" in 1977. PEGGY LEE, RINGO STARR and NINA SIMONE all recorded his songs. He also received two Oscar nominations for his score to the film "Ragtime" in 1981.
British guitarist, singer and songwriter JOHN SPINKS was born in 1955. His first hit was "Your Love" in 1986.
** EVENTS **
1582 : A bond of 40 pounds secured the marriage of
WILLIAM SHAKESPEARE and ANNE HATHAWAY at Stratford upon Avon.
1889 : Mr CURTIS P. BRADY received the first permit
issued by the Commissioner of Parks in New York City to drive an automobile through Central Park. Mr BRADY had to pledge "to exert the greatest care to avoid frightening horses".
1909 : In Paris, a law was passed to allow pregnant women
eight weeks' maternity leave.
1919 : Britains' first woman member of parliament, NANCY
ASTOR, was elected as the member for Plymouth.
1933 : In London, new grounds for divorce were proposed.
They included cruelty, drunkenness and insanity.
1948 : The first polaroid cameras went on sale in Boston.
1950 : The Chinese entered the Korean War. An estimated

200,000 Chinese troops poured over the River Yalu. The Chinese had warned they would react if the United States crossed the 38th parallel into North Korea. The US Eighth Army, marines and South Koreans were forced to retreat.
1967 : All horse-racing was banned in Britain due to an
outbreak of foot and mouth disease.
1971 : In Rome, 100,000 demonstrators marched against
fascism.
1977 : JOHN WINSLOW yo-yoed himself into the record books
by yo-yoeing constantly for 120 hours.
1978 : The Iranian government banned religious marches.
1981 : In New Zealand ROBERT MULDOON retained power,
winning 47 seats to Labour's 43. MULDOON was Prime Minister from 1975 to 1984. The National Party politician pursued austere economic policies such as a wage-and-price policy to control inflation.
1990 : British Prime Minister MARGARET THATCHER resigned.

Mrs THATCHER, who had been Prime Minister since 1979, was the longest-serving leader of the country this century. Her resignation was virtually forced by the resignation of her deputy Sir GEOFFREY HOWE. He was then critical of Mrs THATCHER's hostile attitude to Europe. Her support was flagging as she was forced to a second ballot against leadership challenger MICHAEL HESELTINE. She finally resigned after protracted discussions with senior colleagues. JOHN MAJOR was formally appointed in her place.
